Three days on the Quiet Coast

By the Lantern Trails editors · 9 min read · Updated for the new season

The Quiet Coast is a thin ribbon of cliffs, coves and fishing hamlets that most visitors drive straight past. On foot it opens up. Paths that look like nothing from the road turn into sheep tracks above the surf, and the little harbours appear one at a time, each with a bench placed exactly where you want to sit down.

This route links three of those harbours in three unhurried days. It needs no climbing skill and no special kit, only decent shoes, a rain layer and a willingness to stop for tea. Every stage ends within sight of a place to eat and a bed for the night.

Day one: the lighthouse loop

Start from the car park at the north end of the beach and take the signed path up through the gorse. The first climb is the steepest of the trip, and it ends at the old lighthouse, where the wall makes a good windbreak for a snack. From there the trail follows the cliff edge for six kilometres of easy, rolling ground.

Keep an eye out for the small white marker stones. They were set by the harbour council to show the safe line along the crumbling sections, and they are easy to lose when the mist comes in. If you cannot see the next stone, wait for the mist to lift.

Day two: harbours and hidden beaches

The second stage is the longest, and the most varied. The path drops to sea level at three coves, and you can swim at two of them when the tide is right. Check the tide table before you set off, because the middle cove is cut off for two hours either side of high water.

Nobody hurries on this coast. The harbour clocks are all a few minutes wrong, and everyone agrees that it does not matter.

Lunch is at the net shed in the second harbour, which serves crab sandwiches and strong coffee from a hatch. The afternoon is gentler, with a long, level stretch along the old railway bed before the final descent into the village where you will sleep.

Day three: the long way home

The last day is short on purpose. A shuttle runs from the village to the lighthouse car park at midday, so you can take the high path back in the morning and still be on the road by early afternoon. Most people end up staying for one more cup of tea.
